metadata.note: Boston's rapid transit and subway-surface network – what the MBTA now runs as the Red, Orange, Blue and Green Lines and the Mattapan trolley – from the Tremont Street subway of September 1, 1897 to the Green Line Extension of 2022, including the lines that did not survive: the Charlestown, Washington Street and Atlantic Avenue Elevateds, the Arborway end of the E branch and the Watertown (A) branch. Commuter rail is a separate layer, data/mbta_commuter_rail.geojson. STRUCTURE: each line appears once per physical stage and once per operator (Rule 4) – the West End Street Railway to 1896, the Boston Elevated Railway 1897–1946, the Metropolitan Transit Authority 1947–1963 and the MBTA from 1964 – with the features of one line sharing geometry. CONVENTION: a change is drawn from the calendar year it happened (an extension opened in December is drawn for that whole year, and the stage it replaced stops the year before); every segment note carries the exact date. Ownership years follow the same rule: the MTA took over in August 1947 and the MBTA in August 1964. Green Line branches are drawn from their outer terminal to the Central Subway junction (Kenmore, or Copley for the E branch); the trunk is its own feature. Before 1914 the Beacon Street, Commonwealth Avenue and Watertown cars reached the subway over Beacon Street, Massachusetts Avenue and Boylston Street; that surface link is drawn. Only the streetcar routes that became Green Line branches are drawn; the rest of the Boston streetcar network is not in this layer.
metadata.geometry_source: Modern alignments from the MBTA GTFS shapes (feed "Fall 2026, version D"). Demolished elevateds and street-running sections routed along today's OSM street grid by street name (ODbL); every such feature says so in geometry_quality. Douglas-Peucker simplified at 8 m.
not_yet_sourced: Every historical headway_min is an estimate; no Boston Elevated or MTA public timetable has been checked.
The date the South Huntington Avenue line reached Arborway (after March 1, 1924: "soon extended").
The exact route of the 1901–1908 temporary structure between the Pleasant Street incline and the Washington Street Elevated (drawn as a straight line).
The exact date in 1928 when the south end of the Atlantic Avenue Elevated closed.
Wonderland opening date: January 1954 vs June 19, 1954 (both in the Wonderland station article).
metadata.color_note: MBTA uses #4a4e69, the colour data/mbta_commuter_rail.geojson already gives the agency (Rule 4, one company one colour – the real Red/Orange/Blue/Green line colours are not used). Boston Elevated, the Metropolitan Transit Authority and the West End Street Railway had no colour elsewhere in data/ and were given new ones.
